In short, I run supply chain for a food company in Chile, so about ninety people across four sites. I have been there for eleven years, which surprises everybody including me. At the moment we are closing one of the sites, so, to be honest, this is not the calmest year of my career. That said, the numbers are better than last year. As far as I know, I am the only person here from Chile, so if you want to talk about logistics in a very long country, I am your man. In November I am going to present the site closure as our case, because it is the hardest thing I have ever managed. The point is, I would rather talk about the difficult one than the easy one.

A word about these two-minute introductions, because we do this every year. People think the room remembers job titles. It does not. By Friday, nobody remembers who was a director and who was a head of something. What the room remembers is one number and one problem. If you say ninety people and four sites, that sticks. If you say you are closing a site this year, that sticks, and three people will find you at lunch to talk about it. So when you plan your two minutes, do not polish the title. Pick your number, pick your problem, and say them slowly.
